Admissions Policy
Undergraduate, Graduate, Transfer & International Admission Standards
Document Code: ADM-POL-101
Effective Date: August 1, 2026
Issuing Office: Office of the Registrar & Academic Affairs
Review Cycle: Annual

Meridian State University
Page 2
1. Purpose and Scope
This Admissions Policy governs the criteria, procedures, and timelines by which Meridian State University
("the University") evaluates and admits applicants to its undergraduate, graduate, and professional
programs. It applies to all first-time freshmen, transfer students, readmitted students, non-degree visiting
students, and international applicants.
The policy is designed to ensure that admissions decisions are made fairly, consistently, and in accordance
with applicable federal and state non-discrimination laws. It does not cover financial aid eligibility, which is
addressed separately in the Financial Aid and Fees Policy.
2. Undergraduate Admission Requirements
Applicants for first-time freshman admission must submit a completed application, an official high school
transcript (or equivalent), and, where required by the specific program, standardized test scores. The Office
of Admissions reviews each application holistically, co

3. Transfer Admission
Transfer applicants who have completed 24 or more transferable semester credit hours at a regionally

ursing and Computer Science.
3. Transfer Admission
Transfer applicants who have completed 24 or more transferable semester credit hours at a regionally
accredited institution are evaluated primarily on their collegiate academic record. A minimum cumulative
transfer GPA of 2.5 is required for general admission; select programs, including Engineering and Business,
require a 3.0 minimum in prerequisite coursework.
•
Official transcripts from every institution previously attended must be submitted directly to the Office of
Admissions.
•
A maximum of 90 semester credit hours may be transferred toward a bachelor's degree.
•
Courses in which a grade below C- was earned are not eligible for transfer credit.
•
Transfer credit evaluations are typically completed within 15 business days of receipt of official transcripts.
4. Graduate and Professional Admission

Meridian State University
Page 3
Graduate admission requires a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) from an accredited institution, a minimum
cumulative GPA of 3.0 in the final 60 credit hours of undergraduate study, two to three letters of
recommendation, a statement of purpose, and, for research-intensive programs, a writing sample or
research proposal. Individual departments may impose additional requirements, including GRE, GMAT, or
portfolio submissions, as published in the Graduate Catalog.
4.1 Provisional Admission
Applicants who do not meet the minimum GPA threshold but demonstrate strong potential through
professional experience, recommendation letters, or improved performance in recent coursework may be
admitted provisionally. Provisional students must earn a B or better in their first nine credit hours of graduate
coursework to be converted to regular standing.
5. International Applicants
International applicants must demonstrate English proficiency through an approved standard

rst nine credit hours of graduate
coursework to be converted to regular standing.
5. International Applicants
International applicants must demonstrate English proficiency through an approved standardized test unless
exempted (e.g., completion of a degree taught in English or citizenship of an English-speaking country as
defined by University policy). Upon admission, international students must submit financial documentation
sufficient to cover one academic year of tuition, fees, and living expenses before Form I-20 or DS-2019 is
issued.
•
Credential evaluation through a NACES-member agency is required for degrees earned outside the United
States.
•
Conditional admission with concurrent English-language coursework is available through the Intensive
English Program.
•
International transfer students must additionally submit a SEVIS transfer-in form from their prior institution.

7. Appeals and Reconsideration
Applicants who are denied admission may request a single reconsideration of their file within 30 calendar
days of the decision notification. Reconsideration requests must include new information not previously
available at the time of the original review, such as updated transcripts or test scores. The Admissions

Meridian State University
Page 4
Appeals Committee renders a final decision within 20 business days; its determination is final and not
subject to further institutional appeal.
8. Frequently Asked Questions
Can I apply to more than one program at once?
Yes. Applicants may apply to up to two undergraduate programs or one graduate program per admission
cycle. A separate application and, where applicable, supplemental materials are required for each.
What happens if my transcript arrives after the deadline?
Applications are considered complete only once all required transcripts are received. Late transcripts may
delay review but will not automatically disqualify an otherwise timely application, provided the application
itself was submitted by the stated deadline.
Are interviews required for admission?
Interviews are not required for general undergraduate admission but are a required component of select
professional programs, including Nursing and the Honors College, as noted in their prog

dmission?
Interviews are not required for general undergraduate admission but are a required component of select
professional programs, including Nursing and the Honors College, as noted in their program-specific
requirements.

academic grades across all colleges and schools of Meridian State University. It applies to all credit-bearing
courses, including in-person, hybrid, and fully online offerings.

3. Examination Scheduling
Final examinations are scheduled centrally by the Registrar according to the published final exam matrix and
must not be moved, combined, or administered early without written approval from the relevant Dean's
office. Take-home or online proctored finals must be made available within the same 24-hour window
designated for the course's exam slot unless an alternate arrangement has been approved.
•
No more than two final examinations may be scheduled for a single student within a 24-hour period;
conflicts must be reported to the Registrar within the first two weeks of the term.
•
Make-up examinations require documented justification (medical, family emergency, religious observance,
or University-sanctioned activity).

Meridian State University
Page 3
•
Instructors must retain final examination materials for a minimum of one academic year.
4. Academic Standing and GPA Requirements
4.1 Good Academic Standing
Undergraduate students must maintain a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher; graduate students must maintain
a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher, to remain in good academic standing.
4.2 Academic Probation and Suspension
Students falling below the minimum GPA threshold are placed on academic probation for one term. Failure
to return to good standing, or to meet an individualized academic improvement plan, results in academic
suspension for a minimum of two consecutive terms. Reinstatement following suspension requires a petition
to the Academic Standards Committee.
5. Grade Appeals
A student who believes a final grade was assigned in error, or was based on factors other than the
announced grading criteria, may initiate a grade appeal within 30 calendar days of grade posting. The
appeal proceeds through t

inal grade was assigned in error, or was based on factors other than the
announced grading criteria, may initiate a grade appeal within 30 calendar days of grade posting. The
appeal proceeds through three stages:
•
Stage 1 — Informal resolution directly with the course instructor.
•
Stage 2 — Formal written appeal to the department chair if informal resolution is unsuccessful.
•
Stage 3 — Review by the College Grade Appeals Committee, whose decision is final.
Note: Grade appeals may not be used to contest the academic judgment underlying a grade, only
procedural or factual errors in its calculation or application.
6. Incomplete Grades
An Incomplete (I) may be assigned only when a student has completed at least 75% of course requirements
with a passing average but is unable to finish due to circumstances beyond their control. An Incomplete
Grade Contract must be signed by the instructor and student, specifying the outstanding work and a
completion deadline no later than the end of the f

circumstances beyond their control. An Incomplete
Grade Contract must be signed by the instructor and student, specifying the outstanding work and a
completion deadline no later than the end of the following term. An unresolved Incomplete automatically
converts to an F.
7. Academic Honesty in Examinations
All examinations are subject to the University's Academic Integrity Policy. Suspected violations observed
during an examination, including unauthorized materials, impersonation, or collusion, must be reported to
the Office of Academic Integrity within five business days.
8. Frequently Asked Questions
How is the term GPA different from the cumulative GPA?

Meridian State University
Page 4
The term GPA reflects only courses completed in a single academic term, while the cumulative GPA reflects
all coursework counted toward the degree, including repeated courses under the University's Grade
Replacement policy.
Can I request a regrade of a final exam?
Regrade requests for a final exam must be submitted in writing to the instructor within 10 business days of
grade posting and are limited to demonstrable errors in scoring or point totals, not to a general re-evaluation
of academic judgment.
Does withdrawing from a course affect my GPA?
A grade of W does not carry grade-point value and therefore does not affect the GPA, though it does count
toward attempted credit hours for Satisfactory Academic Progress purposes.

1. Welcome to the University Libraries
The Meridian State University Libraries system comprises the Carrington Main Library, the Science &
Engineering Library, the Fine Arts Reading Room, and the 24-hour Innovation Commons. Together these
facilities hold over 1.4 million print volumes, 220,000 e-books, and subscriptions to more than 48,000
electronic journals, in addition to extensive digital archives and media collections.
This handbook describes borrowing privileges, facility access, research support services, and the policies
that keep library resources available and equitable for the entire campus community.

3. Interlibrary Loan and Document Delivery
Materials not held in the University's collection may be requested through Interlibrary Loan (ILL). Standard
turnaround time is 5–10 business days for physical items and 1–3 business days for scanned articles and
book chapters, delivered electronically at no charge to the requester. Graduate students and faculty
engaged in thesis, dissertation, or funded research may request expedited processing through their subject
librarian.

4. Research and Instruction Services
3.1 Subject Librarians
Each academic college is supported by a dedicated subject librarian who provides one-on-one research
consultations, curates discipline-specific databases, and delivers in-class information literacy instruction.
Consultations may be booked online and are available in person, by video, or by phone.
3.2 Citation and Writing Support

Meridian State University
Page 3
The Library operates a Citation Help Desk offering guidance on APA, MLA, Chicago, and IEEE citation
styles, as well as citation management software including Zotero, EndNote, and Mendeley. Workshops are
held weekly during the fall and spring semesters.
5. Study Spaces and Facility Access
•
Individual study carrels are available on a first-come, first-served basis on Levels 2 through 4 of the Main
Library.
•
Group study rooms (12 total) may be reserved online up to 7 days in advance, for a maximum of 3 hours
per booking.
•
The Innovation Commons is accessible 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, to currently enrolled students with
a valid University ID.
•
Quiet study floors (Levels 3–4) prohibit phone calls and group conversation; collaborative work is directed
to Level 1 or the Innovation Commons.
6. Technology and Equipment Lending
The Library circulates laptops, graphing calculators, DSLR cameras, portable scanners, and charging cables
for short-term loan.

6. Technology and Equipment Lending
The Library circulates laptops, graphing calculators, DSLR cameras, portable scanners, and charging cables
for short-term loan. Laptops circulate for a 4-hour in-library use period or a 7-day external loan for students
who submit a Technology Equity Loan application, prioritized for students with demonstrated financial need.
7. Accessibility Services in the Library
The Library maintains an Adaptive Technology Lab on Level 1, equipped with screen-reading software,
adjustable-height workstations, Braille embossers, and large-print reading equipment. Students registered
with the Office of Accessibility Services may request extended loan periods, priority scanning of course
reserves into accessible formats, and a dedicated liaison librarian to assist with research accommodations.
Requests for materials in alternative formats should be submitted at least 10 business days before they are
needed to allow adequate processi

Requests for materials in alternative formats should be submitted at least 10 business days before they are
needed to allow adequate processing time, particularly for materials requiring conversion from print to
accessible digital formats.
8. Conduct, Fines, and Lost Materials
Patrons are expected to handle library materials and facilities responsibly. Items reported lost are billed at
replacement cost plus a $15 processing fee. Registration holds are placed on student accounts with fines
exceeding $50 or with overdue materials past 60 days, preventing course registration and transcript release
until resolved.
Note: Financial holds related to library fines may be appealed through the Library Fines Appeal Committee,
which meets biweekly during the academic year.
9. Frequently Asked Questions
Can community members borrow books?

Meridian State University
Page 4
Community borrowing cards are available for an annual fee and provide access to circulating collections,
though not to electronic journal subscriptions, which are licensed for current students, faculty, and staff only.
What happens if I lose a library laptop?
Lost or stolen equipment must be reported to Access Services within 24 hours. The borrower is responsible
for the full replacement cost, though a payment plan may be arranged through Student Accounts.
How do I request a book the Library doesn't own?
Use the Interlibrary Loan request form in the library catalog; most requests are fulfilled from partner
institutions within the standard 5–10 business day turnaround.

Academic Integrity Policy
Standards, Violations, Reporting, and Sanctions
Document Code: AIP-POL-415
Effective Date: August 1, 2026
Issuing Office: Office of the Registrar & Academic Affairs
Review Cycle: Annual

Meridian State University
Page 2
1. Statement of Principle
Meridian State University is committed to fostering a culture of intellectual honesty in which all members of
the academic community — students, faculty, and staff — take individual responsibility for the integrity of
their work. Academic integrity is foundational to the value of the degrees the University confers and to the
trust placed in its scholarship.
2. Definitions of Academic Misconduct
2.1 Plagiarism
The representation of another person's words, ideas, data, or creative work as one's own without proper
attribution, whether intentional or resulting from careless citation practice.
2.2 Cheating
Using or attempting to use unauthorized materials, information, or assistance in any academic exercise,
including but not limited to unauthorized collaboration, use of prohibited devices during examinations, and
possession of unauthorized notes.
2.3 Fabrication and Falsification
The invention or alteration of data, citations, or r

unauthorized collaboration, use of prohibited devices during examinations, and
possession of unauthorized notes.
2.3 Fabrication and Falsification
The invention or alteration of data, citations, or results in a laboratory report, research paper, or clinical
record.
2.4 Unauthorized Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools
Submitting work generated substantially by an AI tool as one's own without disclosure, where the course
syllabus or assignment instructions prohibit or restrict such use, constitutes a violation under this policy in
the same manner as unattributed use of any other outside source.
2.5 Facilitating Academic Dishonesty
Knowingly helping another student violate this policy, including sharing exam questions, completing
coursework on another's behalf, or impersonating another student in an exam setting.
3. Reporting Process
Faculty who suspect a violation must document the evidence and submit an Academic Integrity Incident
Report to the Office of Academic Integrity within 10 b

ent in an exam setting.
3. Reporting Process
Faculty who suspect a violation must document the evidence and submit an Academic Integrity Incident
Report to the Office of Academic Integrity within 10 business days of discovery. Students are notified in
writing and given the opportunity to respond within 5 business days before any finding is made.
•
First-time, lower-severity violations may be resolved through a Faculty-Student Resolution Agreement.
•
Repeat or severe violations are referred to the Academic Integrity Board for a formal hearing.
•
Students may be accompanied by an advisor of their choosing throughout the process, though the advisor
may not speak on the student's behalf during hearings.

5. Appeals
A student found responsible for a violation by the Academic Integrity Board may appeal to the Vice Provost
for Academic Affairs within 10 business days of the decision, on the grounds of procedural error, new
evidence, or disproportionate sanction. The Vice Provost's decision is final.

6. Roles of the Academic Integrity Board
The Academic Integrity Board is a standing body composed of five faculty members and two student
representatives, each serving staggered two-year terms and trained annually on hearing procedures and
unconscious bias. A quorum of four members, including at least one student representative, is required to
conduct a hearing.
The Board's role is limited to determining, by a preponderance of the evidence, whether a violation occurred
and, if so, recommending an appropriate sanction from the ranges described in Section 5. The Board does
not have authority to impose sanctions exceeding the ranges published in this policy without written
concurrence from the Vice Provost for Academic Affairs.

7. Faculty Responsibilities
Instructors are expected to clearly state academic integrity expectations, including any course-specific policy
on permitted collaboration or AI tool use, in their syllabi. Faculty should design assessments that reasonably
deter misconduct and must report all suspected violations rather than resolving them unilaterally with an
undisclosed grade penalty.
8. Frequently Asked Questions
Does a first offense always appear on my transcript?
No. Level 1 and most Level 2 sanctions are recorded only in the confidential integrity file. Transcript notation
applies only where suspension or dismissal is imposed.
Can I use generative AI tools for brainstorming even if a syllabus is silent on the
topic?

Meridian State University
Page 4
Where a syllabus does not address AI tool use, students should confirm permitted use directly with the
instructor before relying on such tools, as silence should not be interpreted as blanket permission.
Is a hearing decision by the Academic Integrity Board immediately final?
No. Students retain the right to appeal to the Vice Provost for Academic Affairs within 10 business days, as
described in Section 6 of this policy.

Student Code of Conduct
Community Standards, Conduct Process, and Sanctions
Document Code: SCC-POL-520
Effective Date: August 1, 2026
Issuing Office: Office of the Registrar & Academic Affairs
Review Cycle: Annual

Meridian State University
Page 2
1. Purpose and Authority
The Student Code of Conduct ("the Code") establishes standards of behavior expected of all students at
Meridian State University, both on campus and in University-affiliated activities off campus, including online
conduct that materially disrupts the University's operations or endangers the safety of its community. The
Code is administered by the Office of Student Conduct under the authority of the Vice President for Student
Affairs.
2. Jurisdiction
The Code applies to conduct that occurs on University premises, at University-sponsored events, during
study-abroad or internship placements, and, where the conduct threatens the safety or integrity of the
campus community, off campus. Jurisdiction is not limited by academic term and may extend to conduct
discovered after a student has graduated where a degree was obtained through misconduct.

4. Student Conduct Process
4.1 Initial Review
Reports of misconduct are submitted through the online Incident Report form or directly to the Office of
Student Conduct. A conduct officer conducts an initial review within 5 business days to determine whether
the matter proceeds to a formal resolution process.
4.2 Resolution Pathways
•
Administrative Resolution — an informal meeting between the student and a conduct officer, used for
lower-level violations, resulting in a written resolution agreement.
•
Formal Hearing — used for violations that could result in suspension or dismissal, conducted before a
Student Conduct Board comprising faculty, staff, and student members.
•
Alternative Resolution — restorative justice conferencing, available for eligible cases with mutual
agreement of all parties.

4.3 Standard of Evidence
Determinations of responsibility are made using the preponderance of the evidence standard — that is,
whether it is more likely than not that a violation occurred.

7. Student Rights in the Conduct Process
•
The right to receive written notice of the alleged violation prior to any meeting or hearing.
•
The right to review the evidence supporting the allegation with reasonable advance notice.
•
The right to present witnesses and evidence on their own behalf.
•
The right to be accompanied by an advisor of their choosing throughout the process.
•
The right to a decision based solely on the evidence presented, free from bias or conflict of interest.
•
The right to appeal a Formal Hearing decision as described in Section 7.

8. Appeals
A student may appeal a Formal Hearing decision to the Appellate Board within 10 business days on the
grounds of procedural irregularity, new evidence, or a sanction disproportionate to the violation.
Administrative Resolutions are not eligible for appeal, as they require the student's voluntary agreement to
the outcome.

9. Frequently Asked Questions
Does the Code apply to conduct on social media?
The Code applies to online conduct, including social media, when it materially disrupts University
operations, targets a member of the community with harassment or threats, or otherwise falls within the
jurisdiction described in Section 2.
Will my parents be notified if I am found responsible for a violation?
Parental notification is governed separately by FERPA and applicable state law; in general, notification may
occur for alcohol or drug violations involving students under 21, consistent with federal guidelines.
Can I bring a lawyer to a Formal Hearing?
Students may be accompanied by an advisor, including an attorney, at their own expense; however, the
advisor's role is limited to consultation and does not include direct participation in questioning.

mandatory fees, and manages billing, refunds, and satisfactory academic progress requirements tied to
continued aid eligibility.

3.1 Need-Based Aid
Determined by the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) and includes federal Pell Grants,
Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grants, University Need Grants, and subsidized federal loans.
3.2 Merit-Based Aid
Awarded automatically upon admission based on cumulative GPA and standardized test scores for
incoming freshmen, or upon transfer GPA for transfer students, ranging from $2,000 to full-tuition
Presidential Scholarships.
3.3 Departmental and Graduate Assistantships
Graduate assistantships provide a stipend and full or partial tuition remission in exchange for teaching or
research service, typically 20 hours per week, and are awarded competitively by individual departments.

5. Billing, Payment, and Refunds
Tuition and fee statements are issued each term at least 30 days prior to the payment due date. Students
may elect a five-installment payment plan through the Office of Student Accounts for a $35 enrollment fee.
Accounts not paid in full or covered by confirmed aid by the due date are assessed a 1.5% monthly late fee
and may be subject to a registration hold.

6. Return of Title IV Funds
For students who withdraw and received federal financial aid, the University calculates the amount of
unearned aid that must be returned to the U.S. Department of Education in accordance with the federal
Return of Title IV Funds formula, based on the percentage of the term completed. Students withdrawing
after completing more than 60% of the term are considered to have earned all disbursed aid.
